screens_reviewed: Single capture of app/settings.tsx in dark theme: sticky header (back + 'Settings'), then a scroll with Appearance (theme chips), Text & reading (text-size chips + dyslexia switch), Account (name/email + password note), and a Sign out button at the bottom edge.
verdict: A clean, well-structured settings screen that correctly renders the warm dark palette (background #141513, foreground #F3F1EC, green primary #7FBFA3 on the selected System chip) and consistently uses the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives and useDesignSystem tokens rather than hand-rolled styling. Unlike the audit wizard, dark mode reads correctly here. The main nits are the 40x40 back button (below the 44pt iOS tap-target minimum) and a few inline px/raw-number values where design tokens exist.

improvements.suggestion: The back button is a fixed 40x40 (width={40} height={40}). iOS HIG recommends a >=44pt hit area. Bump to width/height 44 or add hitSlop so the tap target clears the minimum; this is the only navigation affordance in the header.
improvements.evidence: settings.tsx:89-90 (width={40} height={40}); image shows a compact square button top-left

improvements.suggestion: Header uses raw paddingBottom: 12 and the ScrollView passes gap: 28; the layout system exposes sectionGap (20 on phone) and screenPaddingVertical (16) in responsive-layout-tokens.ts. Prefer layout.sectionGap / layout.screenPaddingVertical (or $space tokens) over hardcoded numbers so spacing tracks the responsive tier on iPad.

The header applies paddingTop: insets.top, while the root Stack also injects contentStyle.paddingTop: 20 for every screen (settings registered at _layout.tsx:1389). On a notch device that is insets.top (~59) plus a flat 20, which is why the header sits low in the capture. Consider letting the route own its top inset (e.g. drop the global paddingTop for full-bleed screens) so the header hugs the status bar instead of stacking a fixed 20 on top of the inset.
improvements.evidence: settings.tsx:81 (paddingTop: insets.top); app/_layout.tsx:1376-1379 (contentStyle paddingTop: 20); image shows a noticeable gap between the Dynamic Island and the header row

improvements.suggestion: The toggle is React Native's core Switch styled with palette colors (trackColor/thumbColor). It renders fine, but it bypasses the Tamagui component layer; if a shared Switch/Toggle primitive exists, route through it for consistent press/disabled states and theming. Otherwise this is acceptable.

tamagui_notes: Palette correctness verified: the screen reads colors via useDesignSystem() (settings.tsx:54-55), which returns darkColors in dark mode (lib/design-system.ts:478-487). Screenshot matches — background #141513, surface cards #1E201C, foreground #F3F1EC, green primary #7FBFA3 on the selected System chip and the A/Default text-size chip.

design_system_components_used consistency check passes: every text node uses ScaledText/ScaledParagraph (settings.tsx:102,149,192,245,271,302,346,385) so the auditor's font-scale and dyslexia preferences propagate (ScaledText.tsx:2295-2321). No raw tamagui Text/Paragraph hand-rolled here.
Radii come from the token set (radii.button at :92/:259, radii.lg at :131/:182/:315) per lib/design-system.ts:415-429 — no magic corner values.

Minor: a few inline fixed font sizes (fontSize={22} header at :106, sample sizes 13-21 at TEXT_SIZE_OPTIONS :39-44) are intentional design samples, not token drift; flagged only the spacing constants above.
platform_notes: Safe-area: header pads paddingTop: insets.top (settings.tsx:81) and the ScrollView bottom pad is insets.bottom + 32 (:113), so content clears the Dynamic Island and home indicator. The global Stack contentStyle paddingTop: 20 (_layout.tsx:1378) compounds the top inset — cosmetic, not clipping.

Thumb reach: the primary destructive CTA (Sign out) sits at the very bottom of the scroll (settings.tsx:257-279), within easy thumb reach; the only top-of-screen control is the back button, consistent with iOS.

Compact-fit: the screen reads layout from useResponsiveLayout() and uses getResponsiveContentContainerStyle (settings.tsx:56,112), so it adapts to the phone tier (screenPaddingHorizontal 15) rather than fixed gutters — good.
The Sign out button appears cropped at the bottom of this single capture; with the ScrollView this is a scroll position, not a layout bug.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios (estimated only); muted-foreground #A7A99F secondary text on surface #1E201C looks comfortably above AA for body, but not measured.
Switch pressed/disabled runtime states and the logout transition are not visible in a static capture.
iPad/landscape rendering — only an iPhone dark capture was provided; tablet adaptation via the responsive tokens is inferred from code, not seen.
score_rationale: Solid, ships with minor polish (7-8 band): dark palette is correct, primitives and tokens are used consistently, safe-area and thumb reach are handled. Held below 9 by the sub-44pt back-button tap target and a few hardcoded spacing values plus the compounded top padding, all easy fixes.
